thread:
maya: Morning handoff — quick summary of the last shift. Short version: KV cache paging + unexpected large batcher memory growth caused elevated tail latency and a handful of 5xx errors for the hosted inference pool between ~01:10–02:30 UTC. Pager went out at 01:15.

sergio: Oncall timeline notes — started seeing elevated p95 at ~01:05, alerts tripped at 01:14 (kv_cache_p99_latency > 600ms for 2m). Initial escalation to infra and runtime oncall.

alex: Root cause hypothesis: a client workload with long prompt prefixes and high concurrency triggered a sudden increase in KV memory pressure; eviction lags caused synchronous page faults and backpressure to the batcher. Also saw an increase in small-batch churn which multiplied memory usage.

incident-bot: Pager Acknowledged by sergio at 01:17 UTC.

maya: Mitigations applied by nightshift:
- 01:20: Enabled temporary cache-throttle policy for the affected model route (limit concurrency to 30).
- 01:30: Rolled back the latest runtime micro-change that adjusted kv_evict_threshold (reverted commit 0a1b2c).
- 01:45: Deployed temporary batch_size_cap to 8 via canary to reduce memory growth.
All mitigations in the last hour reduced error rate.

jun: Observed immediate drop in 5xx from ~7% to 0.9% after throttle + rollback. p95 latency down from 750ms to 230ms across the cluster.

maya: Customer impact: small number of long-running requests were retried by clients; we saw 12 distinct customer tokens with >1% error rate during the window. No major contract SLA breaches reported so far. Notifying sales for the 12 customers (handled by CX).

alex: Logs and quick commands if you need to reproduce query surface: 
```
# check eviction stats
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=kv-cache --tail=200 | grep evict
# query metrics
curl -s "${PROM}/api/v1/query?query=kv_cache_evictions_total" | jq .
```

maya: Current status (as of 02:45 UTC):
- Primary mitigations active (cache-throttle + batch cap).
- Error rate stabilized to baseline (0.3% 5xx).
- No open P0 pages. Endpoint health green in console.

sergio: Things that still need attention / follow-ups for the next shift:
1) Long-term fix: tune kv_evict_threshold and optimize lazy-eviction — assigned to infra team (RFC in progress).
2) Add guardrail alert: fire if kv_cache_pages/sec > 200 for >3m (current alerts are focused on latency but not paging volume).
3) Create a test case in perf-suite that simulates long-prefix + high concurrency to catch this earlier.
4) Re-run canary with slightly higher batch_size_cap to measure memory vs latency tradeoff.

maya: Oncall assignment for the next 8 hours:
- Primary: sergio (handles pages & customer escalations)
- Secondary: alex (runtime debugging)
- Pager rotation: jun will cover nights if there's cross-region impact.

maya: Coverage gaps to call out:
- No infra-deep-dive backup engineer flagged between 03:00–09:00 UTC — if something escalates we may need extra hands. If you are on call and available, please reply in-thread.

alex: Runbook pointers:
- KV cache runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache (steps 1–6 for emergency throttle/rollback).
- Batcher troubleshooting: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/batcher-memory (useful commands and dashboards).
- How to revert runtime changes: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/deploy-rollback.

maya: Quick checklist for next shift (copy/paste):
- Verify mitigations are still applied in console (Routes -> MyModel -> throttle = on).
- Watch kv_cache_pages/sec and batcher_memory_gauge for 20m after any config change.
- If error rate >1%: re-enable cache-throttle and notify infra.
- If paging >500/s for >5m: escalate to infra lead + create an incident channel.

jun: Small note: we added a short-lived metric tag to the throttle action so we can track which customers hit the throttle. That will help triage churners.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment succeeded at 01:33 UTC for batch_size_cap change (canary-42).

maya: Outstanding action items (owners + ETA):
- sergio: Create the paging-volume alert rule (+ PR) — ETA EOD today.
- alex: Perf-test case + perf-suite job — ETA tomorrow morning.
- infra (assigned via ticket INF-512): Investigate lazy-eviction flags and recommendation — ETA 2 business days.
- maya: Send CX list to sales for notification — done (01:55 UTC).

sergio: If the next shift is taking over: main logs to check are kv-cache stderr (kubectl logs) and the batcher memory dashboard (Dashboards -> Inference -> Batcher memory). Also check Route-level tokens list for any one customer spamming long prefixes.

maya: Closing note: no outstanding P0, customer notifications in flight, main mitigations are low-risk config toggles. Please escalate immediately if you hit any of the guardrail thresholds above.

alex: acked. I'll be around in the morning for follow-ups.

jun: on it, will watch the dashboards for the next 2 hours.

sergio: Taking primary. thanks all. :thumbsup:
